note: Hand-authored. `quote` is verbatim from https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700 with line wrapping removed and nothing else changed. Not sealed: RFC 9700 is broad and only the waived row below is enumerated. A PKCE row was drafted here and REMOVED rather than kept — no test cites RFC 9700 §4.1.3, and PKCE enforcement belongs under RFC 7636 (a stub in this increment). Marking it covered to make the gate pass would be exactly the over-claiming the gate exists to catch.

requirements.quote: If an authorization code is used more than once, the authorization server MUST deny the request and SHOULD revoke (when possible) all tokens previously issued based on that authorization code.
requirements.reason: The MUST half is satisfied — codes are single-use and a replay is refused with invalid_grant. The SHOULD half is not: QAuth does not additionally revoke tokens already issued from the replayed code, so a token minted by the legitimate first exchange survives an attacker's replay attempt until it expires.
